dk_claim_spiders.description:
North-west of here there's an old goldmine. It was a decent little operation. Gresk ran it, and still runs it after a fashion, and the Undercity liked having it on the books.

Then the spiders came, and now the claim is web and bone and a foreman who hasn't left his own shaft in weeks.

The remarkable thing is that Gresk is still there at all. I'd have written him off and so would you, and he's still standing in the middle of it being extremely rude about his crew's work rate.

Clear the spiders off the claim so the man can breathe. Then talk to him. He'll have his own list, and his list is usually worth hearing.
dk_claim_spiders.accept_text: Burn the webs across the shaft mouths as you go. Gresk won't thank you, but his lungs will.
dk_claim_spiders.turn_in_text:
So he's alive, and still standing in his own shaft complaining.

That's what I hoped. Deathknell needs that mine, and frankly Deathknell needs Gresk, though I'd thank you not to tell him I said the second part.

dk_first_steps.description:
On your feet, good. That's the hard part done, and most of them take longer over it.

I'm Overseer Krell, and I decide what becomes of you now that you've stopped being a corpse and started being a problem. Before you ask the questions they all ask: yes, you were dead. Yes, you're still dead. No, I can't tell you your name, and the ones who go looking for it first tend not to last the week.

Here's what matters today. The body answers now. It just doesn't answer the way it used to, and you won't find that out standing in a graveyard being thoughtful about it.

There are duskbats in the treeline. They're about as gentle a thing as this valley offers. Go and find out what you've got.
dk_first_steps.accept_text: Go north-west, to the treeline by the old goldmine claim, past the last of the graves. Find out what the body still does.
dk_first_steps.turn_in_text:
You're still standing, and you've still got both arms.

That's the whole of today's lesson, and you'd be surprised how many don't manage it. Right, on to the next thing.

dk_gresk_diggers.description:
You're the one Krell sent. Right, don't touch the props, half of them are holding up the other half.

I'm Gresk, foreman of this claim, and before you make the obvious joke: yes, my crew was undead before the spiders came. That's why it was a good operation. They don't tire, they don't drink, and they don't go home.

The trouble is they also don't stop. I gave up supervising when the webs came down, and they just kept going. They're still swinging, still working the face, and now they take a pick to anybody who comes near the shaft, including me, which I'd call ungrateful.

I can't reason with them. I've tried, at length, in a voice I'm not proud of. Try something else.
dk_gresk_diggers.accept_text: They're at the shaft face. They haven't stopped working, and they swing at anyone who comes near it.
dk_gresk_diggers.turn_in_text:
The shaft's quiet now.

He stands in the entrance a while.

They were a good crew, the best I ever had, and I include the breathing ones. Right, don't stand about, there's more wrong with this claim than diggers.

dk_gresk_goldfang.description:
There's one down there that's been eating better than the rest.

The crew called it Goldfang, before the crew stopped talking. It's grown fat on whatever's in that seam and it's gone bright with it. The fangs have come up yellow and they catch the lamplight, which is the only warning you'll get in those tunnels.

It hunts the old workings, my workings, the ones with my crew's marks still chalked on the walls.

Some of the claim spiders run with it. Take those off it first.

And I'll be straight with you. I want it dead because it's in my tunnels, and I want the fangs because they'll fetch a price. Both reasons are real, and I'm not going to pretend only the first one is.
dk_gresk_goldfang.accept_text: Pull the fangs with the roots on. The roots are where the colour goes deepest, and the price with it.
dk_gresk_goldfang.turn_in_text:
That's my tunnels back.

Take a cut of the fangs, and don't argue. A foreman who doesn't pay his crew is a foreman with no crew, and at the moment you're the crew.

dk_gresk_hatchery.description:
This is the last job on this claim, and it's the one that actually finishes it.

In the north-west corner of the Hollow there's a hatchery. Clutches of Brood Hatchlings hang in the silk, rows of them, and a warden called Skrix minds the lot.

On the far side there's the Pale Weaver, which I'd rather you heard about from me than met cold. It doesn't kill what it catches. It spins cocoons around the dead, the already dead, and it goes out and fetches them. Nobody, including me, has a satisfactory explanation for why.

That's Skrix, the Weaver, and the clutches, all of it in one go. Leave any of the three and we'll be doing this again by spring.
dk_gresk_hatchery.accept_text: Burn the clutches, don't break them. Broken eggs still hatch more often than you'd like.
dk_gresk_hatchery.turn_in_text:
He takes the lamp down into the Hollow himself, which he hasn't done since the webs came.

The whole chamber is empty.

That's the claim, genuinely, back on the books and working. Krell's going to be insufferable about it, and he'll have earned it.

dk_gresk_thread.description:
Here's a thing nobody believes until they've seen it, so don't argue, just go and look.

Those spiders weave with gold. I don't mean gold-coloured, I mean actual gold. They've been through the old veins where the face was opened and they're lacing dust through the silk, and in the dark you can see the lines glinting across the whole chamber like somebody's strung a ballroom.

I've no idea why. I've a theory it isn't deliberate and it just sticks to them, which would make it the only stupid thing anything in that cave does.

I want every strand. The Dark Lady likes gold, I like being a foreman the Dark Lady is pleased with, and those two facts are the entire structure of my career.
dk_gresk_thread.accept_text: Go through the web in the old workings. You'll see it glint, you can't miss it.
dk_gresk_thread.turn_in_text:
Gresk weighs a handful on a scale that has seen better decades.

That's a month's output off a seam we'd written off, pulled out of a spider's web by a man who's been dead a fortnight.

I'm going to put that in the return exactly as it happened and let the Undercity make of it what they like.

dk_instructor_bones.description:
You there, come here and pick that up. No, like that. Use both hands until you know better.

I'm the Instructor, and my view is that a Forsaken learns by hitting things that are already dead, because the alternative is learning on things that aren't, and I've buried enough students that way.

The Shadow Grave to the south is full of rattlecage skeletons. They're crypt-dwellers, dead a very long time, and extremely bad-tempered about the fact.

They're the finest sparring partner this valley offers. They never complain, they never tire, and they never stay down, which means you can be wrong four times and still walk back up that hill.

Go and be wrong four times.
dk_instructor_bones.accept_text: Watch their feet, not their weapons. A skeleton always steps before it swings.
dk_instructor_bones.turn_in_text:
That's much better, though you're still slow on the turn, and you drop your guard when you step back, which will kill you eventually.

But it's better. Come back tomorrow and I'll find you something that hits harder.

dk_instructor_ossric.description:
There's one in the Shadow Grave who's a lesson rather than a drill, so listen before you go down there swinging.

Ossric was the sexton. Before any of this, he buried half this village with his own hands, properly, with the rites, in the right order.

Nobody buried him. When it came round to his turn there was nobody left who did that work, and he went into the ground wrong or not at all.

He rises every night among the Wretched Zombies with the spade still in his hand and goes looking for the grave that was never dug for him. He's been at it for years. He's extremely good at digging, and he's never once found it.

So dig it. That's the whole task, and I'd like you to understand it as a kindness rather than a cull.
dk_instructor_ossric.accept_text: If his spade's still whole, lay it beside him. He earned it.
dk_instructor_ossric.turn_in_text:
You put him in it yourself, which is what I hoped.

That's the lesson, and it's the last one I'll give you plainly. You'll spend a long time now among things that can't stop. Some of them need killing. Some of them need finishing. Learning to tell which is the entire art.

dk_instructor_wights.description:
Now for something that'll teach you a distinction nobody in the village will explain properly, because they find it uncomfortable.

Wights are dead and they walk, and that's where the resemblance to us ends.

We were given will. That's the Dark Lady's gift, and whatever anyone thinks of her, that's what she gave. You woke up and you were somebody, however little of him you can remember. A wight got none of that. There's nothing making decisions inside it. It's hunger wearing a shape.

They're among the old stones of the Shadow Grave, and they're drifting up toward the village.

Put them down. And look at one properly while you do, because half of being Forsaken is knowing exactly what you aren't.
dk_instructor_wights.accept_text: Don't let one breathe on you. That cold doesn't wear off for a day.
dk_instructor_wights.turn_in_text:
So, what did you see?

He waits for your answer and nods at it.

That'll do nicely. Most of them say nothing behind the eyes, and most of them say it too quickly. You took your time.

That distinction is going to matter to you more than anything else I teach you.

dk_isolde_keepsakes.description:
I lost more than a husband to this water, though he's the one I came for.

Everybody who mourned here left something. That was the custom. You put a token on the bank when you'd finished saying your piece, a ring or a locket, or ribbon, mostly, from the ones who had nothing else.

The pond-dead have collected them, all of them. I've seen them go along the bank picking the tokens up, and I can't decide whether that's theft or whether something in the pond is hoarding grief. That's the worse thought, and it's the one I keep returning to.

Bring them back up. I'll find the families where there are families. Where there aren't, I'll keep them, and that's better than the silt.
dk_isolde_keepsakes.accept_text: Rinse them in clean water before you bring them up. I'd rather they came home without the pond on them.
dk_isolde_keepsakes.turn_in_text:
She lays them out on her skirt and touches each one.

I know this ribbon. It's the girl from the mill. She came down three days running and never said a word, just sat and left it.

I'll keep them in the box with mine. Somebody ought to know they were left, even if it's only me.

dk_isolde_wren.description:
There's one voice out there louder than the others, and I've been listening to it since the day I arrived.

They call it the Mourning Wren. It stands on the water at night, right on top of it, and it weeps, and every other dead thing in that pond takes up the sound and follows it.

The shades go to her, and that's the part people miss. She isn't the loudest of them, she's the one they're all answering.

I think I know who she is. I'm not going to say it out loud, and I'd be grateful if you didn't ask me afterwards whether I was right.

She's been weeping for years. Let her stop.
dk_isolde_wren.accept_text: If she stops weeping before you reach her, wait. Let her finish.
dk_isolde_wren.turn_in_text:
Isolde listens for a long time before she speaks.

It's quiet now.

You don't have to tell me anything. I'd rather you didn't. I'll sit here tomorrow and the day after and I'll know what I know, and that's mine.

Thank you, I really mean it.

dk_isolde_wretches.description:
Sit, if you like. People don't, usually. They see where I'm sitting and they find somewhere to be.

This pond was a mourners' spot. That's what it was for. You came down here and sat on the bank and said whatever you needed to say to whoever you'd lost, and the water did the listening.

Now the dead talk back. The drowned come up out of the silt, and they moan, and they take hold of anybody near the bank.

I come anyway, every day. I'd like you to understand I'm not being brave about it. I simply have nowhere else to sit that's any better.

But I'd like it quiet while I'm here. I only want it quiet, for an hour.
dk_isolde_wretches.accept_text: They're along the bank and in the shallows. She only wants it quiet for an hour.
dk_isolde_wretches.turn_in_text:
She hasn't moved from the bank.

Thank you. I sat the whole afternoon and nothing came up at all.

I said what I came to say, and the water did the listening, and that's the first time it's worked since I got here.

dk_marrow_shrouds.description:
I'm Sexton Marrow. Mind the trench, that one's spoken for.

I'll tell you my standard, and then you'll understand the request. In thirty years at this yard I've never left anybody uncovered, not one. Plague, Scourge, the lot. Whatever else went wrong up here, everyone who came through my hands went into the ground with linen over their face.

The zombies and the skeletons in the crypt-yard are wearing it. It's my linen, the good stuff, off bodies I wrapped myself, and they've torn it into scraps for no purpose whatsoever.

Get it back for me. I've got a burial on Thursday and I'd be ashamed to use anything less, and ashamed is a strong word for a man in my condition to still have use for.
dk_marrow_shrouds.accept_text: Fold the scraps, don't ball them up. Creased linen is still linen. Crumpled is rags.
dk_marrow_shrouds.turn_in_text:
He folds each scrap along its original crease without thinking about it.

That's enough for Thursday and a little over.

Thirty years and not one uncovered. I intend to keep saying that until there's nobody left to say it to.

dk_neshka.description:
Then we finish it, because a spring doesn't stop running on its own.

Nesh'ka sits at the centre of the Hollow, wrapped in her own silk. Every spider that claim has ever seen came out of her, and while she's down there the cave will keep filling this valley whatever we do at the top end.

Her brood will come at you before she does. They aren't being clever, that's just what a brood is for.

I don't need her negotiated with and I don't need the cave surveyed again. I need a corpse, and I need a handful of the brood brought back so the report has something in it besides my word.
dk_neshka.accept_text: Go back to Night Web's Hollow, the cave beside the claim to the north-west, and this time to its centre. The brood comes first. They always do.
dk_neshka.turn_in_text:
Krell looks at what you've put on the table rather than at you.

That's the claim saved, and that's the valley quiet.

You've been dead about a month. I've had Deathguards take a year to be worth this much trouble.

dk_orrel_scarecrows.description:
Careful of the furrows, they're deeper than they look. I keep meaning to even them out, and then I remember there's no reason to.

My name's Orrel. I tended these fields before the fire and I tend them now, in my own fashion, which I'm aware isn't farming.

The scarecrows I built are walking. They've come down off the frames and they go up and down the rows flailing at anything that moves, which, to be fair, is exactly what I built them to do. I just built them rather better than I meant to, back when I had a reason to be good at it.

So it's my fault. I'd be grateful if you'd correct it, since I can't bring myself to take a hook to my own work.
dk_orrel_scarecrows.accept_text: Burn the straw when they're down. A scarecrow left lying will stand up again by morning.

dk_orrel_seeds.description:
The fire took the house and it took the harvest, and it took the gaffer, near enough.

It didn't take the seed.

I'd buried the packets in the cellar. That's where seed goes, cool and dark, and it's the one bit of sense anybody on this farm ever credited me with. They came through it fine.

Now the burned hands are digging them up. They go down into the cellar and come up with the packets and carry them about the rows, and I honestly think they remember what seed is for.

Get them back for me. Nothing grows in Tirisfal, and I'm not confused about that. I intend to try anyway, and I'd like the trying done properly with the real seed.
dk_orrel_seeds.accept_text: Keep the packets out of the sun on the way back. Seed that's warmed won't sprout.
dk_orrel_seeds.turn_in_text:
He checks each packet is still sealed before he puts it in his coat.

They're all dry, and dry is everything with seed.

I'll put a row in along the south edge where the fire didn't reach the soil. If it comes to nothing I'll have had something to do all spring, and that counts for something too.

dk_orrel_thorne.description:
There's the gaffer, and I've left him till last because I'm a coward about it.

Thorne owned this farm. When the fire came he stayed to save the barn. He sent everyone else down the road and stayed, and when the barn went he stayed anyway, and that's the whole of what happened to him.

He walks the burned rows now with a rusted scythe, cutting down whatever he finds. He thinks it's harvest. You can watch him do it and see the rhythm of it, the proper swing, the step between.

He took me on when nobody else would, and he never once asked why I'd been let go elsewhere.

I owe him a decent burial, and I can't be the one who does it. Some of the hands will be with him.
dk_orrel_thorne.accept_text: Leave him in the rows if you can. He'd want to lie where he worked.
dk_orrel_thorne.turn_in_text:
Orrel has already dug it, at the top of the south edge, by hand.

I got it ready this morning, before I knew. I'd had it in mind for a year.

I'll say the words myself. That bit I can manage. It was only the other bit I couldn't.

dk_risen_grave_dwellers.description:
You can hear it too, can't you? It's the scratching, from underneath.

I don't know my name. I've been told that's normal and that it comes back for some of us, and I've noticed the people who say that don't look at me while they say it.

But I know that sound. It's the only thing I'm certain of in the whole world. That's what it sounds like from the inside, and I made it, and somebody heard me, or I'd still be down there.

The grave-dwellers come up out of the mass pit and wander the field. They aren't coherent. They're where I was a fortnight ago, and some of them won't come further.

Put them back. Gently, if there's a gentle way. I'd want someone to have done it for me if I hadn't come up right.
dk_risen_grave_dwellers.accept_text: Speak to them before you strike. Some of them still turn toward a voice.
dk_risen_grave_dwellers.turn_in_text:
Thank you for that.

I stood out there afterwards and listened, and there was nothing underneath at all. That's the first quiet I've had since I opened my eyes.

dk_risen_grave_markers.description:
A grave marker is supposed to be a name. That's its whole job, one piece of wood that says somebody was here and this is what they were called.

Up here they're mostly splinters, and the restless keep pulling them out of the ground and carrying them off. I've watched them do it. They hold them up. I think they're trying to read them, and I think most of them can't any more.

I want them collected, all the ones you can find.

I know what I'm hoping for, and I know how unlikely it is. But somebody wrote my name on a piece of wood once and hammered it into this hill, and if it's still out there in a dead man's hands I'd like it back.
dk_risen_grave_markers.accept_text: They're out in the grave field. The restless carry them off, so gather what you can find.
dk_risen_grave_markers.turn_in_text:
She goes through them one at a time, slowly, turning each to the light.

It isn't this one, or this one either. No, it's none of them.

That's all right. I'll keep them anyway, because they're somebody's. I'll stand them back up along the fence where they can be read, and whoever comes up next can look.

dk_risen_mawgrin.description:
There's a stray out there that isn't like the others, and I need to ask you for something I can't ask the Overseer for.

He's grey and he's gaunt and he's twice the size of the rest, and he leads them through the graves at night. The villagers call him Mawgrin.

I call him the one who sits on my grave.

He really does. Every night he sits on the open pit where I came up, and he waits. I can't tell you whether he's waiting for me to go back down or for someone else to come up, and I've lain awake deciding which of those is worse.

Some of the pack will be with him. Please deal with him for me.
dk_risen_mawgrin.accept_text: When he's gone, would you fill in the pit? I'd sleep better knowing it was closed.
dk_risen_mawgrin.turn_in_text:
She's been standing at the pit edge.

It's empty now, just a hole in the ground with nothing sitting on it.

I'm going to have it filled in tomorrow. I'll do it properly, with a marker, and I'll put a name on it even if it has to be one I choose myself.

I'm allowed to choose one, aren't I?

dk_scout_hollow.accept_text: Mark the turns with chalk on the way in. Those strands all look the same coming back.

dk_to_brill.description:
The valley's quiet for the first time since you were sewn together, and that means I'm finished with you.

Don't look like that. This is the good outcome. The ones I keep are the ones I can't send anywhere.

Take the road east. It leaves Deathknell for the Tirisfal Glades, and if you follow it through to the portal at the glade's heart it'll put you down at Brill. That's a real town, with a gate and a garrison and people who've been dead long enough to have opinions about it.

This note is for Deathguard Rennick at the gate. It says: take this one, they bite.

I'm not sorry. It's the best reference I've written in two years.
dk_to_brill.accept_text: Don't stop at the portal to admire it. Everyone does, and Rennick gets impatient.
dk_to_brill.turn_in_text:
Rennick reads the note, snorts, and puts it in his coat.

Krell doesn't write references. Krell writes complaints with names in them.

So you'll be useful. Welcome to Brill. Stand over there and try not to look newly risen, because it upsets the carters.

dk_verrick_crypt.accept_text: Keep a light low and your voice lower. The nave carries every sound to the far end.

dk_verrick_fairbanks.description:
High Inquisitor Fairbanks is at the far end of the sanctum, behind a loop of candlelit corridors, and he doesn't leave it.

I'm not going to give you a clever plan because I haven't got one. What I've got is a count: he's broken more Forsaken than this valley currently holds. That isn't rhetoric. I've kept the tally off their own dispatches.

His initiates fill the corridors between, so you won't get a clean run at him.

I've said this to every scout I've sent anywhere: nobody who goes down there should expect to come back.

So far the exception is you. I'd rather it stayed that way, but I'd be lying if I said that was the deciding factor.
dk_verrick_fairbanks.accept_text: Don't answer any question he asks you. He's spent his life getting people to confess.

dk_verrick_halbrook.description:
The sergeant on that line is the reason it holds.

His name is Halbrook. Eight years of service, and he's named his halberd, which I mention not as a joke but because it tells you precisely what sort of man you're walking at.

He isn't angry, he's certain, all the way down, that what we are is a sin and that cleaning it off this valley is simple work that simply has to be done. I've listened to him talk his pickets through it at the change of watch, and he never raises his voice.

I've had him marked longer than anything else in this camp.

His pickets will come in around him, so take those first. The forecourt loses its sergeant, and the line loses its spine.
dk_verrick_halbrook.accept_text: Keep inside his reach once you close. A long blade is slow when the fight is close.
dk_verrick_halbrook.turn_in_text:
The line's gone to pieces. They're standing in threes and looking at the crypt door instead of the valley.

That's what one man was worth. I'd like that noted, because when we write these up we always credit the numbers.

dk_verrick_orders.description:
The Scarlets write everything down.

Dispatches, sermons, duty rosters, orders for the next day's burning, all of it goes on paper, carried on the man, because they've decided that writing a thing down makes it righteous.

I'd call it a weakness if I could stop admiring the discipline of it.

Get me the dispatches off the pickets and the torchbearers. They keep them stuffed in their belts.

A dispatch in my hand tells me what the Crusade intends. What the Crusade intends tells me what to plan against. That's the entire business of scouting, and everybody forgets it in favour of counting tents.
dk_verrick_orders.accept_text: Don't let the ink run. Keep them dry, and keep them flat.
dk_verrick_orders.turn_in_text:
He reads them in order of date, which takes a while.

They aren't here for the valley.

They're here for the crypt, and they were here for the crypt before we ever noticed them. Everything outside is a screen for what's going on under it.

dk_verrick_pickets.description:
Get down behind the rock, there, and don't let the light catch you.

My name's Verrick, and I've been on these rocks a week watching the Scarlet Crusade build a camp outside our crypt.

There are pickets on the line and torchbearers behind them, and a quantity of righteous noise that carries right across this valley at night. They sing hymns. I want you to know that before you go down there, because it's unsettling in a way the fighting isn't.

I've watched long enough to be certain of one thing: they aren't leaving on their own. This isn't a patrol that wandered in. They're digging in.

So we start thinning them, pickets and torchbearers both.
dk_verrick_pickets.accept_text: Go after the hymns stop for the night. They post fewer men when they think God's watching.
dk_verrick_pickets.turn_in_text:
The line's thinner, and they've pulled the torches in closer.

That tells me more than the kill count does. A camp that tightens up is a camp that's started worrying about the dark.

dk_verrick_vaults.accept_text: Open the ossuary first. I've waited longest for those.
